recommended_next_allocator.choice: project adaptation using explicit visible-cell sets only after making those sets real and source-bound; otherwise use a documented Burgard-style scalar visibility utility, not a false union
recommended_next_allocator.assignment_core: For each unassigned robot, choose the feasible task maximizing U_t - beta*C_i_t; initialize U_t from a dimensionless normalized literature-backed utility, use beta=1 only after scale calibration, and reduce other task utility by the documented expected-visible set/region after assignment.
recommended_next_allocator.literal_burgard_warning: Do not call current metre-valued visible_reveal_gain and metre-valued Nav2 path length dimensionally compatible with beta=1. Current gain is a length proxy and current path is a length; subtracting them has no literature-justified meaning unless both are explicitly nondimensionalized/calibrated.
path_scaling_options: preferred: define a dimensionless travel cost C_i_t = path_length_m / calibrated_distance_scale_m, then beta=1 is meaningful only as a declared empirical normalization
alternative: use a measured time estimate path_length_m / shared_nominal_speed_mps, then normalize information utility to the same time/value convention
if exact Burgard utility is desired: implement the paper's utility/cost definitions and document the project-specific conversion separately; do not reuse current AssignmentWeights scales silently
recommended_next_allocator.failure_gate: Filter tasks with active hard suppression before utility ranking; retain expiry/escalation and allow re-entry after bounded TTL or changed physical signature/map evidence. Do not use -5 to make an otherwise infeasible task merely less attractive.
recommended_next_allocator.protocol_impact: No change if the new solver consumes the existing canonical tasks/bids and emits deterministic robot1_task_id/robot2_task_id plus matching fingerprints/hash. Explicit visible-cell union requires a message/data-path extension because current live candidates carry no visible set.
recommended_next_allocator.traffic_boundary: The allocator returns assignments and path samples; a separate traffic gate decides whether a selected goal may be dispatched. It must never make the exploration score encode doorway order.
